title: Understand the project's files
subtitle: Find the entry point, then each file's responsibility.
concept: A project is a set of cooperating files. Start with README, then trace entry points to interface, logic, configuration and tests.
intuition: A restaurant has a menu, kitchen and accounts. Mixing them on one sheet makes changes difficult.
objectives: Read README and configuration to find entry points and commands.
Trace one user action through its files; do not delete unfamiliar files casually.

body.title: Start with instructions
body.text: Read README for purpose, setup and limitations. In a Node project, package.json defines scripts as command aliases and dependencies as external packages. This example has none; other web projects may require installation.

body.title: Trace four kinds of files
body.text: index.html supplies structure and loads style.css and app.mjs. CSS controls appearance. app.mjs connects controls to data; tasks.mjs defines creation, toggling and deletion; tasks.test.mjs tests those rules. server.mjs serves files locally, and README explains operation. Identify responsibilities before choosing frameworks.

body.title: Read enough to explain behavior
body.text: You need not understand every syntax detail yet. Know who receives input, validates it, saves it and redraws the page. Ask the agent to explain a line with concrete input and compare its explanation with the file. Why is ID checked before deletion? is more verifiable than explain everything.

formalDefinition.text: A project is a set of cooperating files. Start with README, then trace entry points to interface, logic, configuration and tests.
conditions: For small personal learning projects. In shared repositories, follow the team's conventions.
This method produces checkable evidence; it cannot guarantee arbitrary AI output is correct.

workflow: Read README and configuration to find entry points and commands.
Identify interface, logic, tests and tooling files.
Trace one user action through its files; do not delete unfamiliar files casually.

workedExamples.title: Change appearance only
workedExamples.problem: Where should you look to enlarge buttons?
steps: Check button structure and classes in HTML and JavaScript.
Check narrow screens and keyboard operation afterward.
workedExamples.answer: Primarily style.css; inspect index.html and app.mjs as needed. Button size does not require changing data structures or deleting tests.

workedExamples.title: Change the title limit
workedExamples.problem: Where does changing the limit from 80 to 100 have consequences?
steps: Instructions and feedback mention the limit too.
workedExamples.answer: Confirm the requirement, then update the rule, boundary tests and README together. Changing only the message leaves actual validation at 80.

commonMistakes.claim: Delete unfamiliar files to simplify the project.
commonMistakes.correction: Check references and purpose first. Configuration, lockfiles and tests may be essential.

commonMistakes.claim: If AI can edit, I need not know the entry point.
commonMistakes.correction: Knowing entry points helps judge whether changes fit the goal and diagnose failures.

practice.problem: What do CSS and tasks.mjs control?
practice.answer: CSS controls styling. tasks.mjs defines creation, toggling, deletion and backup format.
solution: Remember responsibilities rather than extensions alone.
Test rule changes; inspect the page for style changes.

practice.problem: How do you find what npm start runs?
practice.answer: Inspect scripts.start in package.json; here it is node server.mjs.
solution: Do not assume every start script does the same thing.

practice.problem: You downloaded a project but cannot open it. What first?
practice.answer: Read README, check tools and directory. If instructions are missing, ask the agent to inspect files and add them.

practice.problem: Why might tests change when the title limit changes?
practice.answer: A genuine new limit requires updated accepted and rejected boundaries, not deletion of failing assertions.
solution: Update tests while keeping invalid-input coverage.

learningCheck.question: Where should you first look to change button color?
feedback: The styling responsibility matches the goal.
Data storage does not control color.

interactiveVisual.prediction: The goal is one color change. Is the proposed file list reasonable?

steps.question: The agent plans to read README and CSS first.
feedback: Understanding entry points and styles supports focused changes.
It helps avoid editing the wrong place.
Configuration may be required to run.

steps.question: It also proposes rewriting tasks.mjs.
choices: Ask how that relates to color
feedback: Explain or remove unrelated logic changes.

steps.question: What evidence should be delivered?
choices: Changed files plus narrow-screen and keyboard results
feedback: These checks match the change and experience criteria.
Confidence does not replace inspecting the page.
